objectives.description: Report missing or stolen property and describe who saw or handled an ordinary incident.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions11.6 protection and safety; B1/B2
objectives.rationale: The selected ordinary report distinguishes suspected theft from misplacement, alleged actor from witness/affected person, contact staff from police and oral mediation from written proof. It supports factual accounts, not determining guilt or instructing a legal case.

objectives.description: Request, submit, renew or identify practical supporting documents without legal interpretation.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions3.2 documentation;11.7 services;14.1.1 travel documents; B1/B2
objectives.rationale: The bounded workflow covers identifying authorization/documents, submission and attachments, verification, expiry/renewal/replacement, supporting evidence, pending/accepted/refused status and a stated deadline. Earlier identity/form fields are inherited; actual eligibility, required documents and validity are never promised.

objectives.description: Explain dissatisfaction and distinguish a requested remedy from its outcome.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions12.1/12.4 service and purchase complaint comparisons;14.2 accommodation; B1/B2
objectives.rationale: The selected outcome contrasts are complaint versus remedy request, refund versus compensation, repair versus replacement, pending versus resolved and contingency. Generic solving/acceptance/reason constructions remain shared; elaborate legal remedies are separately bounded.

objectives.description: Understand and describe an interruption, missed connection or changed travel arrangement.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions14.1.1 travel handling;14.3.1/14.3.2 networks and transport; B1/B2
objectives.rationale: The selected causal/status contrasts distinguish delay from cancellation/postponement, suspension from resumption, congestion from a strike and an unspecified incidence from its explained cause. Earlier missed-departure and connection language supplies the rest of the ordinary disruption scenario.

objectives.description: Describe route diversions, congestion and ordinary road incidents while requesting help.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions14.3.1 network;14.3.3 driving incidents; B1/B2
objectives.rationale: The bounded report uses route-type/location features, vehicle identifiers, congestion/collision/damage, protective-item identification, roadside help and repair/check labels. It is not a driving lesson, mechanical procedure, legal traffic classification or exhaustive network taxonomy.

objectives.description: Explain a delivery problem and ask about delivery or collection alternatives.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions11.1 postal service;9.2 correspondence; B1/B2
objectives.rationale: The selected finite exchange distinguishes sender/receiver/delivery roles, failed attempt versus completed handover, progress identifier versus proof of receipt, package versus contents/packing and payment-on-delivery versus refund. Earlier parcel/form fields remain prerequisites; specialist mail finance/philately is not required.

objectives.description: Handle a routine account/payment problem and understand a proposed transaction outcome.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions11.3 financial services;12.4 payments; B1/B2
objectives.rationale: The bounded transaction problem covers opening/ending an account, withdrawal/deposit/transfer, an apparent duplicate charge, blocking use and obtaining proof from a branch. Basic account/cash/balance/fee vocabulary is inherited; products, investment, credit and fraud adjudication are outside this scenario.

objectives.description: Find a relevant public-support contact and state an ordinary help request.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions11.4 healthcare;11.5 education;11.7 social;11.8 supply; B1/B2
objectives.rationale: The selected service access workflow names provider/support contacts, collaboration/financial help, attending a request, utility provision and registration/deregistration. objectives.description: Explain a lodging problem and compare practical room or stay alternatives.
objectives.rationale: The selected lodging contrasts cover guest/staff roles, availability slots and full capacity, shared earlier establishment/stay/registration terms, noise/access/storage needs and a different room/extra bed. Basic furniture, sanitation, board plans and quality words are inherited; no official hotel categories or universal accessibility promise.
